Subject: VPC connectivity - integration & network next steps

Hi Raj / Anika,

Thanks again for the productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the FinPay integration:  

Summary of needs from the call:
- Private connectivity from FinPay VPC to Redwood endpoints (VPC endpoints / PrivateLink or customer NAT egress path)
- IP allowlist for egress and optional inbound allowlist for webhook callbacks
- Egress DNS resolution and outbound TLS inspection constraints (FinPay runs an outbound proxy)
- mTLS for mutual auth on the private endpoint (preferred)
- SDK auth: short-lived tokens via your identity provider (OIDC) or long-lived API keys for server-to-server calls
- Routing: stable model endpoint hostnames + fallback to hosted variants for burst capacity
- Embeddings + reranker: we will recommend colocated KV cache and persistent storage considerations
- Structured output / tool calling: JSON schema enforcement and validation hooks to avoid unexpected outputs

Proposed next steps:
1) FinPay network team to share the network diagram and preferred connectivity option (we can support VPC Endpoint, IP allowlist over public egress with TLS, or Private Deployment).
2) Redwood to provide a concise integration checklist and example VPC endpoint and mTLS config (I asked Jonas to include the initial technical notes below).
3) Schedule a follow-up technical sync next week with your NetOps and our infra team (30-45 min).
4) I'll attach a starter SOW and network diagram request form for procurement.

Attachments: I attached a sample network diagram template and a draft SOW for your procurement team to look at.

Questions for FinPay before the tech call:
- Do you prefer VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) or outbound allowlist with NAT egress?
- Are you able to present a public CA-signed cert for mTLS, or do you require mutual cert rotation via an internal PKI?
- Any egress DNS interception or outbound proxy that rewrites SNI/hostname?

Thanks \u0014 happy to coordinate times.

Best,
Lauren Bishop

Thanks Lauren \u0014 great summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:  

- We prefer a PrivateLink/VPC endpoint approach for production traffic but may use public egress for non-sensitive bursts during initial testing.
- Our platform requires mTLS for any inbound private endpoints; we can provide certs via our internal PKI. We'll need guidance on cert format and rotation expectations.
- We do have an outbound proxy that performs TLS inspection in some regions; please advise on SNI and DNS implications.

Attaching our high-level network diagram for the call. Can Jonas share the example VPC endpoint security group rules, IP ranges Redwood expects to allow, and a sample mTLS handshake sequence? That will help our NetOps prepare.

Let's plan for a technical sync on Wednesday 2027-06-02 at 10:00 AM PT if that works for your engineers.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: VPC connectivity - integration & network next steps (technical notes)

Hi Raj / NetOps,

Thanks for the diagram \u0014 quick technical notes to make the upcoming sync productive. High-level options we support and recommended defaults: 

1) VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink) - recommended for production
- Provision a consumer VPC endpoint that connects to Redwood Private endpoints. We expose a regional private hostname per model route.
- Security groups: allow outbound HTTPS (443) from Redwood subnets to your endpoint ENIs. On your side, allow inbound from Redwood ENI CIDR blocks.
- IP ranges: for initial allowlist, you can use our documented regional CIDR blocks (we will provide exact list per region).

2) Public egress + IP allowlist - acceptable for staging/testing
- Ensure outbound NAT rules allow traffic to our public IP ranges; we sign TLS with a CA cert and recommend validating CN/SAN.
- If you have an outbound proxy that rewrites SNI, please whitelist by IP and ensure TLS passthrough for model endpoints.

3) mTLS considerations
- We support mTLS mutual auth on the private endpoint. We accept PEM-encoded cert chains and private keys for initial provisioning; for long-term, we recommend automating rotation via your PKI or ACME flow.
- Handshake: client cert must present a leaf cert signed by your CA. Our servers validate client cert chains against the CA bundle you provide.
- We also support token-based client auth (OIDC/OAuth2 client credentials) as an alternative if mTLS is not feasible.

4) DNS and egress behavior
- For PrivateLink, DNS mapping will resolve to private IPs in your VPC. If you are using outbound proxy/DNS interception, ensure private DNS is enabled for the VPC endpoint.
- For staged public egress, use the SNI hostname we surface; if SNI is rewritten, rely on IP allowlist instead.

5) SDK and auth notes
- SDK supports short-lived OIDC tokens (recommended) and legacy API keys. We provide a server-side refresh example in Node and Python in the integration checklist.
- For embeddings/reranker traffic, we recommend colocated batching with persistent cache on your side to reduce token costs and round trips.

6) Structured output and tool calling
- We'll add a validation layer in the request pipeline to enforce response JSON schemas for tool-calling. This can be toggled per-route during rollout.

Next steps for the sync: we'll prepare a 1-page network configuration template and the regional CIDR list. Please share expected maintenance windows and whether you prefer pre-shared certs or an automated provisioning flow.

Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
